trust_decision.summary: A client-supplied 'scope' regex (from the extraHttpHeaders form field) is compiled with the backtracking regexp2 engine and no match timeout. It is then run against every sub-resource URL that Chromium requests. The fix bounds the match time of that client regex.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the extraHttpHeaders scope feature, and the only regexp2.Compile of client input is in the extraHttpHeaders Custom parser.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/modules/chromium/chromium.go:410 (public Options.ExtraHttpHeaders []ExtraHttpHeader{Scope *regexp2.Regexp}) consumed unguarded at pkg/modules/chromium/events.go:108

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Go library callers that build Options directly supply their own regex, so they are trusted, and the advisory concerns the HTTP form field only.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate scoped headers must still apply. A valid scope regex (for example one with lookarounds, which regexp2 supports) must match and set the header. A non-matching URL must not get the header. Switching to RE2 or rejecting the scope feature would break these .NET-style patterns.

O6_input_shapes: scope token inside the extraHttpHeaders JSON value string ('value;scope=<regex>'), with any whitespace or case variant of 'scope' accepted by pkg/modules/chromium/routes.go:178-183

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A client-supplied regex-based filter (for example a scope or pattern on cookies or failOnResourceHttpStatusCodes domains) compiled with regexp2 and no timeout.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same parser already uses regexp2 on client JSON (sameSiteRegexp), and ignoreResourceHttpStatusDomains is a natural place for a pattern-matching feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-header scope regex on Gotenberg-Webhook-Extra-Http-Headers, mirroring the chromium scope syntax.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The webhook already parses an extraHttpHeaders JSON map with the same shape, in another package, so copying the scope feature would be natural.

services: Chromium (headless) for end-to-end; parser-level unit tests need none
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/modules/chromium/routes_test.go (FormDataChromiumOptions table tests); pkg/gotenberg/filter_test.go; test/integration (godog, needs Docker)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set p.MatchTimeout on the compiled scope regex (the published fix), or replace regexp2 with stdlib RE2, which breaks lookaround scopes.

out_of_scope_notes: Operator allow/deny lists (pkg/gotenberg/flags.go:212,238) are regexp2 with no compile-time timeout, but they are operator-controlled. pkg/gotenberg/filter.go:26-27 applies a deadline at match time.

Even with a 5s timeout, many scoped headers multiplied by many sub-resource requests can still add up (pkg/modules/chromium/events.go:100-108). This is resource exhaustion, a non-lever per lessons-v2.
unverified: sameSiteRegexp (pkg/modules/chromium/routes.go:26-29) runs on client cookie JSON with no MatchTimeout. The pattern is fixed and looks linear, so I judged it not a ReDoS route, but this was not analysed formally.
Whether the scope match also runs for the main document request or only for intercepted sub-resources was not traced beyond pkg/modules/chromium/events.go.
O12: I did not flag single_site because the O2 lower_level_api site is recorded. That site is weak (it is trusted library input), and if it is discounted, single_site applies.
Recall risk is a judgement: the advisory was published in 2026-04 with a one-line fix.
